newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol declares Eindhoven airport takeover plan.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol declares Eindhoven airport takeover plan.

text.p: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport has declared its intention to take a stake of 51 percent in Eindhoven Airport, a Schiphol spokeswoman said.
Both airports are expected to sign a memorandum of understanding for the new relationship before the Dutch government's summer recess, she added, without giving details of proposed financial terms.
Schiphol is aiming to encourage more flights into the southern Dutch airport to improve its profitability, a joint airport statement said. Presently, weekend and night flights are restricted.
Currently, Eindhoven Airport is owned by Eindhoven City and the Province of North Brabant municipal council.
Under the proposed new deal, a separate enterprise will be created for real estate and the industrial area around Eindhoven airport.
In this enterprise, Eindhoven City will have a 51 percent share and Schiphol, 49 percent. A new industrial park is expected to cover a 60 hectare site.
Additionally, Eindhoven and Schiphol said they aim to double the amount of passengers using Eindhoven airport in the next 20 years to approximately 500,000.
